I'll carefully compare source and draft, hunting for signature losses.

**Key findings:**

1. **"But though thus contrasting within, the contrast was only in shades and shadows without; those two seemed one; it was only the sex, as it were, that distinguished them."** — The paragraph resolving the air/sea gender contrast is entirely absent from the draft. This is a rhetorically distinctive closing to the opening cosmological metaphor.

2. **The passage "did at last seem to joyously sob over him"** — The source reads "did seem to joyously sob over him"; the draft omits "joyously sob over him" and elides the full phrase, losing the voice-distinctive emotional register.

3. **Several lines from Ahab's speech are cut**: "forty years on the pitiless sea!" and "only half-suspected, not so keenly known to me before" and "when the poorest landsman has had fresh fruit to his daily hand, and broken the world's fresh bread to my mouldy crusts" and "here, brush this old hair aside; it blinds me, that I seem to weep. Locks so grey did never grow but from out some ashes!" and "By the green land; by the bright hearth-stone! this is the magic glass, man" and "No, no! not with the far away home I see in that eye!" — some of these are high-signature passages.

4. **Starbuck's full speech is truncated** — "How cheerily, how hilariously, O my Captain, would we bowl on our way to see old Nantucket again! I think, sir, they have some such mild blue days, even as this, in Nantucket." is cut, including the transition to Ahab's response.

5. **"Albicore" / "Where do murderers go, man! Who's to doom, when the judge himself is dragged to the bar?"** — This is cut from Ahab's final monologue. It is critically engaged, interpretively weighty, and distinctively voiced.

6. **"nor one single star can revolve, but by some invisible power"** — trimmed from the draft's version of the fatalism speech.
